learning_objective: 🎯 Master the traffic signals of writing that tell your reader exactly when to stop, pause, or show big excitement!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A Full Stop (.) is a red light telling the reader to stop completely at the end of a sentence. A Comma (,) is a yellow light telling the reader to just slow down, take a tiny breath, and pause.
Use a Question Mark (?) only when you are asking for information. Use an Exclamation Mark (!) when you want to show a sudden burst of strong emotion, like extreme joy, shock, or fear!
The Apostrophe (') has two main jobs. It shows ownership, like 'Rahul's book'. It also acts like a hook to catch missing letters when we squish words together, like changing 'do not' into 'don't'.
Quotation Marks or Inverted Commas are like little fences. They trap the exact words that are coming out of someone's mouth. Example: My mom shouted, 'Time for dinner!'

fun_activity.title: 😮 The Breathless Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Write a long paragraph about your day without using a single punctuation mark. Give it to a friend and tell them to read it out loud without stopping for a breath!

quick_recap: ⭐ Punctuation marks are the road signs of writing; they organize sentences and make them make sense.
⭐ Commas separate items in a list, while apostrophes show who owns something or combine two words into a contraction.
